title: Steering hard to turn
h1: Why is my steering suddenly hard to turn?
metaDesc: Steering suddenly heavy or stiff? Find out if it's power steering fluid, a belt, an electric steering fault or tires, how urgent it is, and what to tell your mechanic.
synonyms: power steering went out while driving
hard to steer at low speed
intro: Power steering is what makes the wheel easy to turn. When it suddenly feels heavy, the assist has usually dropped out, and how it happened tells you a lot about why. Answer the questions below to narrow down possible causes and how urgently to get it looked at.
safety: If the steering suddenly goes heavy while driving, grip the wheel firmly with both hands, slow down gradually, and pull over when it's safe. Steering usually still works without assist, but it can take much more effort.
If the temperature gauge climbs toward the red at the same time, pull over and turn off the engine. A broken belt can stop the cooling system too.
If you smell burning fluid or see smoke from under the hood, turn off the engine and step away from the car.

q_how.q: How did the steering become hard to turn?

opts.a: Suddenly, while I was driving or right after starting
Gradually over days or weeks, mostly when parking or at low speed
It's stiff for the first few minutes on cold mornings, then gets easier
It catches, sticks or binds at certain points as I turn
I'm not sure

q_sudden_signs.q: Did anything else happen at the same time?

opts.a: The engine stalled or shut off
A loud squeal or slap from the engine, or the battery light came on
A steering wheel warning light or a 'power steering' message came on
Nothing else I noticed
I'm not sure

q_fluid.q: With the engine off, check the power steering fluid reservoir under the hood. What do you find?
q_fluid.help: The reservoir is usually a small plastic tank with a cap marked with a steering wheel symbol. Many newer cars have electric power steering with no fluid at all; your owner's manual will say.

opts.a: The fluid is low, or there's fluid leaking under the front of the car
The fluid looks full
My car doesn't have a reservoir (electric power steering)
I'm not sure
A whine or groan when I turn the wheel, louder at full lock
The front tires look low or soft
A creak, pop or clunk when I turn, especially over bumps
None of these, it's just heavier than it used to be
I'm not sure

q_warning.q: Is a steering wheel warning light or a power steering message showing on the dash?
q_warning.help: It often looks like a steering wheel with an exclamation mark, and may be yellow or red.

opts.a: Yes
No
I'm not sure

result.title: The engine stopping cut your power steering. The stall is likely the main problem
result.now: Get the car somewhere safe and don't use it until the stalling is diagnosed. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If it restarts and the steering feels normal again, the stall is the more likely cause, but have both checked. The stalling alone makes the car unsafe in traffic.
If it won't restart, follow our car won't start guide while you wait for help.
result.why: Power steering only works while the engine is running (or, on electric systems, while the car is fully on). When the engine dies, steering and brakes both get much heavier. Fixing the stall fixes the steering.

causes.name: Engine stalling from a fuel, sensor or idle problem
causes.clues: Sputtering, rough idle or a check engine light before it died.

causes.name: Charging system failure
causes.clues: The battery light came on or lights dimmed before it stalled.

causes.name: Broken accessory belt
causes.clues: A squeal or slap from the engine, and the temperature gauge rising.

you: Note any warning lights that were on before the stall.
Check whether the belt at the front of the engine is still in place (engine off, keys out).

result.title: The accessory belt may have slipped off or broken
result.now: Turn off the engine and don't run it again until the belt is checked. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If the temperature gauge was rising, the belt may drive the water pump too. Running the engine could overheat it badly.
If the belt is in place but badly glazed or cracked and squealing, it may be slipping. Have it checked before the car is used; a shop will usually check the tensioner and pulleys at the same time.
If you smell burning rubber or see smoke from the front of the engine, turn it off and step away from the car.
result.why: On many cars one belt drives the power steering pump, the alternator and often the water pump. When it breaks, you lose steering assist, the battery stops charging, and the engine can overheat within minutes.

causes.name: Broken or thrown accessory (serpentine) belt
causes.clues: A loud slap or squeal, then heavy steering and a battery light.

causes.name: Failed belt tensioner or seized pulley
causes.clues: A squeal or chirp in the days before, or a pulley that wobbles.

causes.name: Seized power steering pump or other accessory
causes.clues: A grinding noise before the belt failed.

you: With the engine off and keys out, look at the front of the engine for a missing or loose belt.
shop: Accessory spin check for a seized component
Charging system and cooling system check after repair

result.title: The electric power steering system may have shut off its assist
result.now: Once you're safely parked, turn the car off for a minute and restart. If the warning stays on or the steering is still heavy, have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If the warning clears after a restart and steering feels normal, don't assume it's fixed. Have the stored fault code read before relying on the car.
If the battery light is also on, low voltage may be shutting the steering off. The charging system needs checking.
If the assist drops out again while you're driving, grip the wheel firmly, slow down gradually and pull over when it's safe.
result.why: Electric power steering uses a motor to help you turn. When it detects a fault or low voltage, it shuts the assist off, and the wheel suddenly takes much more effort. It can come back and fail again without warning.

causes.name: Low battery voltage or charging problem
causes.clues: A battery light, dim lights, or a recent dead battery.

causes.name: Steering sensor or control module fault
causes.clues: The warning comes and goes, and steering feels normal when the light is off.

causes.name: Failed steering assist motor
causes.clues: The warning stays on and the steering stays heavy after restarting.

you: Note exactly which warning lights came on.
Check for open recalls on your car using your VIN on the NHTSA recalls site. Steering assist problems are a common recall topic.
shop: Steering assist motor and sensor tests

result.title: Low power steering fluid from a leak is a possible cause
result.now: Don't use the car until the leak has been looked at. Topping up with the fluid type in your owner's manual may bring the assist back for a while, but a leak big enough to drop the assist suddenly can do it again. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If you see fluid spraying, smell burning fluid or see smoke from under the hood, turn off the engine and step away from the car.
If the pump whines loudly even after topping up, it may already be damaged. Tell the shop.
If the steering ever binds or catches as you turn, keep the car parked.
result.why: The power steering pump needs fluid to create pressure. When the level drops, assist fades, and running the pump low can damage it. Topping up can buy time, but a leak usually comes back, and power steering fluid dripping onto hot engine parts can burn.

causes.name: Leaking power steering hose
causes.clues: Wet, oily hoses near the pump or along the front of the engine.

causes.name: Leaking steering rack seals
causes.clues: Fluid inside the rubber boots at the ends of the steering rack, or drips behind the front wheels.

causes.name: Leaking pump seal
causes.clues: Fluid around the pump at the front of the engine.

you: Check the fluid level with the engine off.
Put cardboard under the front of the car overnight to see where it drips.

result.title: The power steering pump, belt or steering rack may not be providing assist
result.now: Don't use the car until it's diagnosed. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If the belt at the front of the engine is missing or loose, the belt is the more likely cause. Tell the shop what you saw.
If the steering also binds or catches, it may be a more serious steering fault. Keep the car parked.
result.why: If the fluid is full but the assist suddenly disappeared, the pump may not be making pressure or the rack may not be using it. Steering usually still works, but it takes much more effort, which is dangerous in an emergency move.

causes.name: Failed power steering pump
causes.clues: A whine or groan in recent weeks, or foamy fluid.

causes.name: Slipping or broken belt
causes.clues: A squeal, or the belt looks loose, glazed or missing.

causes.name: Internal steering rack failure
causes.clues: Steering is heavier in one direction than the other.

you: With the engine off and keys out, look at the belt at the front of the engine.

result.title: Sudden loss of power steering needs checking before you rely on the car
result.now: Keep the car parked and have it towed or call a mobile mechanic to find the cause.
if: If the temperature gauge rose or the battery light came on, a broken belt is a strong possibility. Don't run the engine.
If a restart brings the steering back to normal, still have the fault diagnosed. It may happen again.
result.why: When steering assist drops out suddenly, the cause is usually a failure, not wear, and it can happen again at a bad moment. Without assist, quick steering moves take much more strength.

causes.name: Electric power steering fault or low voltage
causes.clues: A steering or battery warning light.

causes.name: Broken or slipping belt
causes.clues: A squeal, or the battery light came on too.

causes.name: Low fluid or failed pump (hydraulic systems)
causes.clues: Whining when turning, or fluid under the front of the car.

you: Look under the front of the car for fresh fluid.

result.title: A whining pump often means low fluid or a pump that's wearing out
result.now: Check the power steering fluid level with the engine off. If it's low, top it up with the type in your owner's manual and have the system checked within a few days. If the reservoir is empty, have it inspected before driving.
if: If the fluid was low, there may be a leak. Ask the shop to find it before the pump is damaged.
If the steering suddenly gets much heavier, binds, or a steering warning light comes on, stop driving and have it towed.
If you see fluid spraying or smell burning fluid, turn off the engine and step away from the car.
result.why: A whine or groan when turning often means the pump is struggling, sometimes because it's drawing in air from low fluid. Left alone, it can wear out the pump and leave you with no assist.

causes.name: Low power steering fluid
causes.clues: Fluid below the minimum mark, or drips under the front of the car.

causes.name: Worn power steering pump
causes.clues: The whine stays even with the fluid full.

causes.name: Slipping belt
causes.clues: A squeal on cold starts or when turning at full lock.

you: Check the fluid level and color. Dark or foamy fluid is a bad sign.
Look under the front of the car for drips.

result.title: Low front tire pressure can make steering feel heavy
result.now: Check the tire pressures when cold and set them to the numbers on the driver's door jamb sticker.
if: If a tire keeps losing air, have it repaired soon.
If steering is still heavy with correct pressures, have the steering system checked.
If the steering suddenly becomes much heavier, binds, or a steering warning light comes on, stop driving and have it checked before going further.
result.why: Underinflated tires put more rubber on the road, which makes the wheel harder to turn, especially when parking. Pressure is quick to check, but it may not be the only cause.

causes.name: Low tire pressure
causes.clues: The tires look soft or the tire pressure light is on.

causes.name: Wider or different tires than original
causes.clues: New tires or wheels were fitted recently.

causes.name: Wheel alignment out of spec
causes.clues: Uneven tire wear, or the car pulls to one side.

you: Check and set all four tire pressures.
shop: Power steering system check if the problem stays

result.title: Worn or dry steering and suspension joints may be making it stiff
result.now: Have the front suspension and steering inspected within the next few days.
if: If you hear a loud clunk and the steering suddenly feels loose or different, stop driving it and have it towed. A failing ball joint can let a wheel collapse.
If the noise only happens on cold mornings and goes away, it may be strut mounts. Still have it checked.
If the steering binds, sticks at certain points or doesn't return to center, keep the car parked until it's inspected.
result.why: Ball joints, tie rod ends and strut mounts let the wheels turn smoothly. When they wear out or lose their grease, they can bind and creak, which makes steering feel stiff and can lead to a part failing. A shop will usually check for play in each joint before deciding which part needs work.

causes.name: Worn or dry ball joints
causes.clues: Creaking when turning or going over bumps, and uneven tire wear.

causes.name: Worn strut mounts or bearings
causes.clues: A pop or clunk when turning the wheel while parked.

causes.name: Worn tie rod ends
causes.clues: Loose or wandering steering on the highway.

you: Turn the wheel slowly while parked with the window down and listen for where the noise comes from.
shop: Ball joint and tie rod play check

result.title: Wear in the power steering system or front end is a possible cause
result.now: Check the tire pressures and power steering fluid (if your car has it), then book a steering inspection.
if: If the steering suddenly becomes much heavier or a steering warning light comes on, stop driving and have it towed.
If you start to hear whining or clunking, get it checked within a few days.
If the steering binds, sticks or feels loose, stop driving and have it inspected first.
result.why: Steering that slowly gets heavier often comes from wear rather than a sudden failure: low tire pressure, a tired pump, worn joints or a steering rack losing efficiency. A shop can test each of these to narrow it down.

causes.name: Low tire pressure
causes.clues: Tires look soft, or the tire pressure light comes on.

causes.name: Worn power steering pump or old fluid
causes.clues: Dark fluid, or it's worse when the engine is cold.

causes.name: Worn steering rack or suspension joints
causes.clues: Creaks, uneven tire wear, or a wheel that doesn't return to center easily.

you: Check the power steering fluid level and color if your car has a reservoir.

result.title: Something in the steering is binding. It needs checking before you drive
result.now: Don't use the car until the steering is inspected. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If it only catches slightly right after the car has been parked with the wheels turned, it may be the steering lock or a sticky shaft joint. It still needs checking.
result.why: Steering that sticks at certain points instead of turning smoothly can stop you from steering where you need to go. It usually means a part in the steering column, shaft, rack or front suspension is seizing or damaged.

causes.name: Sticking steering shaft joint
causes.clues: A notchy or catching feel in the steering wheel, often at the same spot.

causes.name: Seizing ball joint or tie rod end
causes.clues: Creaking, and the steering doesn't return to center on its own.

causes.name: Damaged steering rack
causes.clues: A recent curb or pothole hit, or it binds in one direction only.

shop: Ball joint and tie rod inspection

result.title: Old fluid or a tired pump often makes steering stiff when cold
result.now: Check the power steering fluid level and color if your car has a reservoir, and book a check when convenient.
if: If the stiffness lasts longer each day or you hear whining, get it checked within a few days.
If a steering warning light comes on, have it checked before driving further.
If the steering stays heavy after the engine is warm, or it binds or suddenly gets heavier while driving, stop and have it checked before driving further.
result.why: Power steering fluid thickens in the cold. Old or low fluid, or a pump that's wearing, may not keep up until things warm up. On electric systems, a weak battery on cold mornings can do the same.

causes.name: Old or low power steering fluid
causes.clues: Dark fluid, or the level is near the minimum mark.

causes.name: Wearing power steering pump
causes.clues: A groan or whine while it's stiff.

causes.name: Weak battery (electric power steering)
causes.clues: Slow cranking on the same cold mornings.

you: Check the power steering fluid level and color.
Note whether the engine cranks slowly on those mornings.
shop: Power steering fluid and pump check
